req.title: Return 404 on unknown post
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 when GET/POST /<id>/update or /<id>/delete references a non-existent post id.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-022 requires HTTP 404 when GET/POST /<id>/update or POST /<id>/delete references a non-existent post id. Tests must: (1) confirm 404 for a clearly non-existent id on both update and delete endpoints (NEG/EP), (2) confirm 200 for an existing post id on update GET (positive/EP), (3) probe the boundary between the highest existing post id (20) and the next id (21) which does not exist (BVA), (4) cover the decision table of method × endpoint × existence (DT), and (5) cover state transitions from logged-in to 404 response (STC). All tests log in as user Rahul (id=1) who owns posts 2,3,6,8,9,10,11,12,15,18,19,20 per the pre-loaded data.

tests.name: test_update_get_nonexistent_post_returns_404
preconditions: App initialised with pre-loaded database
User Rahul (id=1, password='stone') is logged in
Post id 9999 does not exist in the database
trace: R-FLASKR-022: GET /<id>/update with non-existent id must return 404
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

with client.session_transaction() as sess:
    pass

r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
assert r_login.status_code == 302, f'Login failed: {r_login.status_code}'

r = client.get('/9999/update')
assert r.status_code == 404, f'Expected 404, got {r.status_code}'
assert b"doesn't exist" in r.data or b'404' in r.data
